passage:
A school considered using software to watch students during online exams. The software could track eye movement, noise, and other behavior.
Some teachers liked the idea because cheating was a concern. Students worried about privacy and unfair judgments. A student with anxiety said being watched by software would make testing harder.
The school chose a different approach: shorter oral checks, open-book questions, and project-based exams.
The debate showed that trust and assessment are connected.
A system designed to stop cheating can create new problems if it treats every student as suspicious. Good testing measures learning without ignoring dignity.
